exec: Political pressure is building over the outages; officials uniformly say no cyberattack is involved.
plain: US politicians want answers about the run of outages. The President, the spy chief, the homeland security chief and the White House all say it was not a cyberattack.

sources.name: BNN Bloomberg / CTV News live updates

summary: Lawmakers are pressing for answers after outages at Microsoft, the FAA, banks, Apple and the NSA. Trump, DNI Clayton, DHS Secretary Mullin and the White House say they see no cyberattack. On 18 November Mullin, Clayton and FBI Deputy Director Raia repeated this to a House committee; Nextgov and CyberScoop report many lawmakers link the outages to rushed patching of AI-found flaws.
title: Washington reacts to the outages: lawmakers demand answers, DHS chief points to AI

validation.note: Political response reported by The National Desk, Newsweek, Nextgov and CyberScoop; hearing of 18 Nov read at Nextgov and CyberScoop.
